events.title: Henry V Crowned Holy Roman Emperor
events.description: Henry V was crowned Holy Roman Emperor in Rome by Pope Paschal II after a dispute over lay investiture, during which Henry had taken the pope captive to force concessions.
events.significance: The event was a key moment in the Investiture Controversy, the medieval struggle between secular rulers and the papacy over the appointment of church officials.

events.title: Edict of Nantes Signed
events.description: King Henry IV of France issued the Edict of Nantes, granting French Protestants (Huguenots) substantial rights and freedom of conscience in a predominantly Catholic country.
events.significance: It was one of the earliest major steps toward religious tolerance in Europe and helped end the French Wars of Religion.

events.title: Birth of Thomas Jefferson
events.description: Thomas Jefferson was born in Shadwell, Virginia. He became the principal author of the Declaration of Independence, the third President of the United States, and orchestrated the Louisiana Purchase.
events.significance: Jefferson's ideas about liberty, republican government, and westward expansion profoundly shaped the early United States.

events.title: Fort Sumter Surrenders
events.description: After a 34-hour Confederate bombardment, Union Major Robert Anderson surrendered Fort Sumter in Charleston Harbor, South Carolina.
events.significance: The surrender marked the first battle of the American Civil War, prompting Lincoln to call for volunteers and leading more Southern states to secede.

events.title: Apollo 13 Oxygen Tank Explosion
events.description: Two days into its mission to the Moon, an oxygen tank exploded aboard the Apollo 13 service module, forcing the crew of Jim Lovell, Jack Swigert, and Fred Haise to abort the lunar landing and improvise a return to Earth.
events.significance: The crew's safe return, achieved through ingenuity and teamwork by NASA, became known as a 'successful failure' and a landmark in spaceflight crisis management.
